text:
[name]
Tempe, AZ · [email] · [phone] · [url] · [url]

OBJECTIVE
I am a highly motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science student at Arizona State University with a strong passion for software development, problem solving, and learning new technologies. I am seeking a summer 2027 software engineering internship where I can apply the knowledge I have gained in my coursework and personal projects to real-world problems, contribute to a collaborative team environment, and continue to grow as an engineer under the mentorship of experienced professionals.

Throughout my academic career I have developed a solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, and web development, and I have consistently challenged myself to go beyond the classroom through independent projects, hackathons, and student organizations. I believe my combination of technical skills, strong work ethic, and enthusiasm for technology would make me a valuable addition to any engineering team, and I am excited about the opportunity to bring my skills to an innovative company.

EDUCATION
Arizona State University, Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering — Tempe, AZ
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, expected May 2028
GPA: 3.5/4.0 · Dean's List: Fall 2024, Spring 2025, Spring 2026

COURSEWORK
CSE 110 – Principles of Programming: Introduction to programming in Java covering variables, control flow, methods, arrays, and basic object-oriented design. Final project was a text-based inventory management program.
CSE 205 – Object-Oriented Programming and Data Structures: Classes, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, generics, linked lists, stacks, queues, and recursion in Java. Weekly programming assignments and two exams.
CSE 230 – Computer Organization and Assembly Language: MIPS assembly, number representation, memory hierarchy, and the datapath. Wrote a small assembler as the final project.
CSE 240 – Introduction to Programming Languages: Programming paradigms using C, Scheme, and Prolog; parsing, scoping, and memory management in C.
CSE 310 – Data Structures and Algorithms: Asymptotic analysis, sorting, hash tables, balanced trees, graphs, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, and dynamic programming. Implemented a graph library in C++.
CSE 330 – Operating Systems: Processes, threads, synchronization, scheduling, virtual memory, and file systems. Lab assignments included a user-level thread library and a simple shell.
CSE 340 – Principles of Programming Languages: Lexical analysis, parsing, type checking, and interpreters; wrote a recursive-descent parser and an interpreter for a small language.
CSE 360 – Introduction to Software Engineering: Requirements, UML, agile methods, version control, and testing. Semester-long team project (see Projects).
CSE 365 – Information Assurance: Security principles, cryptography basics, authentication, access control, and common vulnerabilities.
MAT 243 – Discrete Mathematical Structures: Logic, proofs, sets, relations, functions, counting, and graph theory.
MAT 343 – Applied Linear Algebra: Matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues; MATLAB assignments.
STP 420 – Introductory Applied Statistics: Probability, hypothesis testing, and regression in R.
Currently enrolled (Fall 2026): CSE 412 Database Management; CSE 445 Distributed Software Development; CSE 475 Foundations of Machine Learning.

PROJECTS
Campus Study Group Finder (CSE 360 team project, team of 5, Spring 2026) — Java, JavaFX, SQLite, GitHub
A desktop application that lets students post and join study groups for their courses. I served as the team's Scrum master and was responsible for the database schema and the data access layer. We used a two-week sprint cadence with GitHub Projects for tracking, wrote JUnit tests for the data layer, and presented the final product to the class. I learned a great deal about coordinating a team, resolving merge conflicts, and writing documentation for teammates. Final grade on the project: A.

Weather Dashboard (personal project, Summer 2025) — JavaScript, React, Node.js, Express, OpenWeather API
A single-page web application that displays the current weather and a five-day forecast for any city entered by the user, following a React tutorial series and then extending it. I added a favorites list stored in the browser's local storage, a dark mode toggle, and a small Express backend that caches API responses to stay under the free-tier request limit. Deployed to a free hosting platform. This project taught me the basics of React hooks, asynchronous requests, REST APIs, and deploying a full-stack application.

Sudoku Solver and Generator (personal project, Winter 2025) — Python, Tkinter
A desktop Sudoku application with a backtracking solver, a puzzle generator with three difficulty levels, and a simple graphical interface built in Tkinter. The solver uses constraint propagation before backtracking, which made solving most puzzles nearly instant. I wrote unit tests for the solver with pytest and documented the algorithm in the README. I built this to practice recursion and algorithm design after taking CSE 310.

Personal Portfolio Website (ongoing) — HTML, CSS, JavaScript
A static website showcasing my projects, resume, and blog posts about what I am learning. Built from scratch without a framework to practice responsive design and accessibility basics.

EXPERIENCE
Sales Associate, Best Buy — Tempe, AZ (June 2025 – Present, part-time, about 16 hours per week)
• Assist customers in the computing department with laptop, tablet, and accessory purchases, explaining specifications and comparing products.
• Set up and troubleshoot demo devices on the sales floor and help with inventory counts.
• Recognized as a top-five associate in the department for customer satisfaction survey scores in Q4 2025.

Peer Tutor, ASU Engineering Tutoring Center — Tempe, AZ (August 2025 – Present)
• Tutor students in CSE 110 and CSE 205 during drop-in hours, about 6 hours a week.
• Help students debug Java programs and understand object-oriented concepts.

Volunteer Instructor, Code for Kids Tempe (Summer 2024)
• Taught introductory Scratch programming to middle school students in a two-week summer camp.

STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS AND ACTIVITIES
• Software Developers Association (SoDA) at ASU — Member since Fall 2024; attend weekly technical talks and workshops; participated in the Fall 2025 internal hackathon (built a campus event recommendation prototype in 24 hours with three other students).
• ACM Student Chapter — Member; attended the Spring 2026 programming competition practice sessions.
• Women in Computer Science (WiCS) — Ally member; volunteered at the Spring 2026 high school outreach day.
• Sun Devil Hackathon (Fall 2025) — Participant; team built a recipe-suggestion web app from pantry ingredients; did not place.
• Intramural soccer — Team captain, Fall 2025 and Spring 2026 seasons.
• Residence hall community council — Floor representative, 2024–2025 academic year; helped plan two floor events per semester.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming Languages: Java (proficient), Python (proficient), C/C++ (intermediate), JavaScript (intermediate), HTML/CSS, SQL (basic), MIPS assembly (coursework), Scheme and Prolog (coursework), MATLAB (coursework), R (coursework)
Frameworks and Libraries: React, Node.js, Express, JavaFX, Tkinter, JUnit, pytest
Tools: Git and GitHub, VS Code, IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, Linux command line, SQLite, Postman, Figma (basic)
Concepts: Object-oriented design, data structures and algorithms, agile/Scrum, unit testing, REST APIs, basic networking and operating systems

CERTIFICATIONS AND ONLINE COURSES
• Responsive Web Design Certification, freeCodeCamp (2025)
• JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures Certification, freeCodeCamp (2025)
• Introduction to Machine Learning, online course (audited, 2026)
• AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials, online course (in progress)

INTERESTS
Hiking and backpacking (four Arizona summit hikes), soccer, chess (online rating around 1400), building mechanical keyboards, science fiction novels, cooking, playing guitar, and hobby game development (currently learning Godot).

REFERENCES
Available upon request.
